subject.title: [Bug]: sessions_spawn child runs fail after acceptance with HTTP 401 Missing scopes api.responses.write

question: Should native `sessions_spawn` child runs inherit the requester session's effective provider/model/runtime/auth profile by default, require an explicit inherit path, or stay isolated and fail fast when the child route cannot execute?
rationale: Current source only carries model metadata into the child path while another session creation path copies fuller runtime/auth state; choosing the default changes provider routing, auth-profile persistence, and subagent isolation semantics.

options.title: Inherit effective route/auth by default
options.body: Carry the parent effective provider/model/runtime/auth profile into native child runs when no explicit subagent route is configured, and add fail-fast validation plus regression coverage.

options.title: Make inheritance explicit
options.body: Land an explicit inherit mechanism such as the open model-inheritance PR first, then add a separate auth-profile inheritance or validation decision.

options.title: Keep child routes isolated
options.body: Do not inherit parent auth/runtime state, but validate the resolved child route before accepting the spawn and return a direct missing-scope/auth error.

recommendation.title: Inherit effective route/auth by default
recommendation.body: Carry the parent effective provider/model/runtime/auth profile into native child runs when no explicit subagent route is configured, and add fail-fast validation plus regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled history across subagent spawn planning, control-boundary, and auth-profile state paths.
